Primary: CNBC quote endpoint, read 08:11 BST.

*** SUNDAY — EVERY MARKET EXCEPT BITCOIN IS SHUT, SECOND DAY RUNNING ***
Nine of the ten instruments carry Friday's closes, identical to Saturday's edition. CNBC reports UNCH or a
self-referential change on a closed day, so the figures below are the Friday session moves computed against
Thursday's closes, exactly as yesterday, and the drivers say explicitly that markets are closed.

BITCOIN is the only live price and the only figure that has moved since yesterday's edition: 83,054.67
against Friday's close of 82,322.43 = +0.89. Saturday's edition published 82,752 (+0.52 on the same basis),
so bitcoin has risen about 300 overnight. CNBC's own change_pct field reads +0.08, which is measured against
a rolling intraday reference rather than Friday's close; +0.89 is published so that every instrument on the
weekend ticker is on the same basis.

CARRIED UNCHANGED FROM SATURDAY (Friday's closes, Friday's session moves):
  FTSE 10,552.05 +1.06 | SP 7,811.54 +0.59 | Brent 104.72 +0.42 | GBP 1.3231 +0.05 | Gold 4,193.83 +1.45
  EURGBP 0.8464 +0.04 | Gilt 5.44 +0.01 | VIX 14.84 -3.70 | UST 5.24 +0.01
The gilt remains the declared figure from Friday's close: CNBC's final Friday read was 5.4226 stamped after
the cash market shut, Trading Economics gave 5.45, and 5.44 is the number taken live at 18:02 on Friday.
That spread of 5.42 to 5.45 stands unresolved until Monday.

TWO SUPPLY SHOCKS NOW SIT ON OPPOSITE SIDES OF THE OIL PRICE, both recorded in the Brent driver:
  Bearish — the US has suspended sanctions on Russian diesel to 7 April, with 300,000 tonnes promised
    immediately and up to 4.8m in total.
  Bullish — twelve killed at Riyadh airport on Saturday, a US jet disabling a tanker in the Gulf of Oman,
    and about 69% of US Gulf of Mexico output still shut after Hurricane Isaias, with the Energy Department
    authorising an emergency release of up to 4 million barrels.
Brent settled Friday before most of this. Monday's open is the first real read.
